Conclusion: the notice rules differ.

India Handbook: provident fund under the EPF Act; employee 12%, employer 12%, plus optional VPF.
UK Handbook: private medical insurance after probation, with dependent coverage not specified.
India Handbook: group medical insurance for all employees, covering spouse and up to two children, with optional parent top-up.
Conclusion: the benefit structures are different.

questions.short_answer: The UK Handbook adds shared parental leave and longer maternity/adoption leave, while the India Handbook gives 26 weeks of maternity leave and 12 weeks of adoption leave with a third-child reduction for maternity.
key_points: UK Handbook includes shared parental leave up to 50 weeks.
UK Handbook provides up to 52 weeks of adoption leave and 52 weeks of maternity leave.
India Handbook provides 26 weeks of maternity leave, reduced to 12 weeks for the third child onwards.
India Handbook provides 12 weeks of paid adoption leave for a child below 3 months.
Conclusion: the family-leave packages are different.

questions.ground_truth: UK Handbook: standard full-time hours are 37.5 per week. India Handbook: standard full-time hours are 40 per week. Notice may be given by either party; it is 30 days during probation, or as stated in the appointment letter, and 60 days after confirmation, or as stated in the appointment letter. Therefore, the India Handbook has a longer standard workweek by 2.5 hours, and the notice frameworks differ: the UK Handbook is based on length of service with a cap, while the India Handbook is based on probation/confirmation status and appointment-letter terms.
questions.short_answer: The India Handbook’s standard workweek is 2.5 hours longer, and notice is service-length based in the UK Handbook but probation/confirmation and appointment-letter based in the India Handbook.

India Handbook: 40 standard full-time hours per week.
